kypExtensions.summary: The pattern/trap/pivot/mini-case attack structure layered over the source's AUTONOMIC/SOMATIC diagram.
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid supplies the diagram and its labels; the attack structure is a KYP design.

kypExtensions.summary: The three-anchor reading of the diagram (ANCHOR 1 — COUNT THE NEURONS: two neurons (preganglionic + postganglionic, meeting at a ganglion) is AUTONOMIC — smooth muscle, gland cells, nerve terminals, cardiac muscle; one neuron (the voluntary motor nerve) is SOMATIC — skeletal muscle. ANCHOR 2 — NAME THE GANGLIONIC SYNAPSE: it is ALWAYS ACh on Nn, in BOTH divisions and at the adrenal medulla — the diagram prints ACh at every ganglion and Nn beside it; this is why a ganglionic (Nn) blocker silences both divisions at once while sparing the neuromuscular junction. ANCHOR 3 — READ THE POSTGANGLIONIC TRANSMITTER: it names the receptor alphabet at the organ — ACh → M₁, M₂, M₃ (parasympathetic targets) or M₃ (sweat glands); NE → α1, α2, β1, β2; D → D1 (renal vasculature); and the adrenal medulla, the axon-less endocrine limb, pours Epi + NE into the 'Blood (catecholamine transmission)' onto α1, α2, β1, β2 at cardiac muscle and vessels) — KYP's synthesis of the scattered diagram labels into one reading order (count neurons → name the ganglionic synapse → read the postganglionic transmitter).
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the diagram labels spatially without a reading protocol; the three-anchor order, the neuron-count test, and the transmitter-names-the-receptor-alphabet rule are KYP's design.
kypExtensions.location: core.keyIdea + mechanisms + the visual's reading-rule strip

kypExtensions.summary: The three sympathetic exceptions grouped into one panel (1 — SWEAT GLANDS: sympathetic pathway, cholinergic fiber, M₃ receptor — the source's own footnote 3 ('Sweat glands are part of the sympathetic pathway but are innervated by cholinergic fibers') and its diagram labels (ACh → M₃ → Sweat glands); 2 — RENAL VASCULATURE: a dopaminergic sympathetic branch, D → D1 (the diagram's own labels); 3 — ADRENAL MEDULLA: no postganglionic neuron at all — directly innervated by preganglionic sympathetic fibers (the source's own footnote 2), secreting Epi + NE into blood). The facts are the source's own; the grouping into a three-exceptions panel and its exam exploitation (which drug blocks sweat, which vasodilates the kidney, which endocrine organ answers preganglionic ACh) are KYP's design.
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the three exceptions as scattered labels and footnotes; the grouping and the selective-therapy angle are KYP's synthesis.
kypExtensions.location: mechanisms[1] + usmle patterns + the visual's exceptions panel

kypExtensions.summary: The four KYP-original mnemonics (1 — THE GANGLION IS ALWAYS NICOTINIC: every autonomic ganglion and the adrenal medulla sit behind ACh on Nn; only the organ synapse changes. 2 — PARA = LONG P, SHORT POST; SYM = SHORT P, LONG POST: the parasympathetic ganglion sits ON the organ, the sympathetic chain NEAR the cord. 3 — THE SYMPATHETIC EXCEPTIONS: SWEAT IS M₃, KIDNEY IS D1, ADRENAL HAS NO AXON. 4 — TWO NEURONS TO THE ORGANS, ONE TO THE BONES: autonomic pathways are two-neuron chains ending on M/α/β/D receptors; the somatic voluntary motor nerve is a single neuron ending on Nm at the neuromuscular junction). The Autonomic receptors section prints NO margin mnemonic — all four codes are KYP-original designs.
kypExtensions.rationale: Book 234's Autonomic receptors section prints NO mnemonic; all four codes are KYP-original designs.

notes: Census (pdfimages + VLM): NO raster images on the page (pdfimages -list returned zero rows for pdf 256). The Autonomic receptors section is a VECTOR LINE-ART diagram — path-drawn nerves, ganglia, and organs with typeset labels in the PDF text layer — plus three typeset footnote lines. The diagram is redrawn as an ORIGINAL_KYP_REDRAW (an original KYP SVG with original KYP glyphs: the CNS band, the three pathway columns, the synapse chips, the organ plates) — no source artwork is reproduced; the labels carried across are short attributed anatomical/neurotransmitter terms (ACh, NE, Epi, D, Nn, Nm, M₁-M₃, α1/α2/β1/β2, D1, organ names). PAGE-RANGE FINDING: the section does NOT continue onto pdf 257 — pdf 257 (book 235) opens the SEPARATE section 'Acetylcholine receptors' (the next pending topic) under the same banner, so sourcePages stay [256] (book 234); the boundary is pinned as a 257-side evidence item. The book's printed 'chold' sweat (sic — ie, a 'cold' sweat) is carried verbatim and flagged [sic] wherever quoted. The clinical anchors that extend past the source page (ganglionic blockers trimetaphan/mecamylamine; glycopyrrolate-neostigmine reversal pairing; pheochromocytoma and α-before-β blockade; renal-dose dopamine and fenoldopam; β3/mirabegron as the adrenergic receptor beyond this diagram's printed set; the Nn-vs-Nm selectivity of hexamethonium-type vs rocuronium-type blockers) are flagged as KYP clinical anchors wherever they appear. No copyrighted photographs exist on the page; nothing reproduced. EXCLUSION: the 'Drug effect modifications' section in the UPPER portion of this SAME page is the COMPLETED topic PH10 ('drug-effect-modifications') and is EXCLUDED from this topic: PH11 pins the same source page (pdf 256 / book 234) for its LOWER portion only.
